activation: Active root *.patch: all qualities and preparation host OSes, in shell-glob order after root JSON removals and before Insider/OS/user patches. Effective only for the surviving target surface.
effect: Three coordinated macOS changes: package the internal launcher as bin/<applicationName>, point the PATH-install symlink at that renamed file, and return the renamed file from the built CLI-path API. VSebCode deliberately keeps bin/code internally while installing /usr/local/bin/vsc; its package path, symlink target and CLI-path API agree. Windows and Linux already derive their launcher names from applicationName and are not changed by this patch.
gaps: No port needed under the recorded internal-launcher decision. Renaming only one of the three sites would break the other callers.

activation: Active root *.patch: all qualities and preparation host OSes, in shell-glob order after root JSON removals and before Insider/OS/user patches. Effective only for the surviving target surface.
effect: Adds twelve experimental font family/size settings for the workbench, activity bar, bottom pane, sidebars, status bar and tabs, shared clamped/scaled font metrics, configuration application, CSS variables and fallback inheritance. It scales shared controls, component geometry, pane/header/notification heights, virtualized lists/trees, editor find widgets, debug/extensions/explorer/SCM/search/notebook/preferences/process/remote/testing/timeline views, terminal tab rows and modern-UI layouts; it adds metric tests and adapts layout tests. None of the central settings/metric module or the surviving component integrations is present in VSebCode. The patch spans 98 target files: 86 existing fork files, two new font files absent, and ten intentionally removed AI/session target files. Detailed behavior mapping is in build.md.
gaps: Optional interface/accessibility feature missing on the actively validated macOS platform as well as the other desktop platforms.
Porting only the twelve settings or font-family CSS would omit layout/virtualization behavior. Removed chat/session adaptations are intentional exclusions.
No visual rendering or font-change interaction test was run; this is source-level coverage, not a claim that the VSCodium implementation is bug-free.

activation: Active root *.patch: all qualities and preparation host OSes, in shell-glob order after root JSON removals and before Insider/OS/user patches. Effective only for the surviving target surface.

The installed signer carries Microsoft-specific license terms; this is dependency evidence, not a legal determination.

activation: Active root *.patch: all qualities and preparation host OSes, in shell-glob order after root JSON removals and before Insider/OS/user patches. Effective only for the surviving target surface.
effect: Changes Debian version from packageVersion-linuxRevision to packageVersion, removes RPM release-token substitution, changes Snap displayed version from commit prefix to packageVersion, and strips VSCodium timestamp suffixes from vscode.version exposed to extensions. VSCodium get_repo.sh appends a four-digit day/hour suffix; the later Linux RPM patch replaces @@RELEASE@@.el8 with el8, completing the removed token replacement. VSebCode uses ordinary 1.143.0 and upstream revision conventions, so the Debian/RPM/API normalization is INAPPLICABLE to its current version scheme. The independent human-readable Snap version effect is MISSING: fork Snap still uses eight commit characters.
gaps: Optional Snap version presentation differs; Linux packaging validation is deferred.
No basis to adopt VSCodium timestamp versioning or its API regex wholesale.

activation: Active root *.patch: all qualities and preparation host OSes, in shell-glob order after root JSON removals and before Insider/OS/user patches. Effective only for the surviving target surface.
effect: Product-update effect INTENTIONAL: adds update.minReleaseAge default 120h, bypass at zero, rejection for missing/invalid timestamps and rounded absolute release age gating; fork updater is deleted. Extension effect PARTIAL: adds extensions.minReleaseAge default 48h to Extension.outdated for newer versions, using rounded absolute age and zero bypass. VSCodium applies that gate on top of the upstream autoUpdateDelay path already present at its pinned base. VSebCode retains the upstream configurable 12h auto-update delay, with trusted-publisher/forceAutoUpdate bypasses and no delay for missing/future timestamps, but it has no 48h outdated gate. Manual update visibility and timestamp edge behavior therefore differ.
gaps: Default ordinary-extension automatic delay is shorter than VSCodium (12h versus its additional approximately 48h gate). Setting existing extensions.autoUpdateDelay=48 would cover the ordinary auto-update waiting intent without reproducing all semantics.
The current tracked product has no trustedExtensionPublishers list; that bypass exists in code but should not be reported as configured.
The VSCodium rounded-absolute-age gate can differ by half an hour and treats future timestamps differently; no claim that its algorithm is inherently safer.

activation: Active root *.patch: all qualities and preparation host OSes, in shell-glob order after root JSON removals and before Insider/OS/user patches. Effective only for the surviving target surface.

activation: Active root *.patch: all qualities and preparation host OSes, in shell-glob order after root JSON removals and before Insider/OS/user patches. Effective only for the surviving target surface.
effect: Replaces policy-watcher 1.4.0 with @vscodium/policy-watcher 1.4.0-265896 and synchronizes native binary packaging, imports, lint/test/performance fixtures and lockfile dependencies. Passes ORG_NAME to regular and AI managed-settings watcher APIs. Separately rewrites Windows ADMX registry vendor prefix and namespace, macOS PayloadOrganization/default organization, application/documentation URLs and profile description URLs. VSebCode has newer upstream watcher 1.6.0 but still uses its default Microsoft Windows prefix and renders Microsoft policy namespaces/organization/enterprise URLs. Its macOS bundle/domain is already VSebCode; AI managed-settings code is deliberately removed. Upstream 1.6.0 already supports an optional registryPath, so behavior can be implemented without downgrading to the older fork.
gaps: Surviving policy metadata branding is a concrete macOS gap. Windows runtime/generator vendor prefix also remains Microsoft, although Windows validation is deferred.
Any future change must keep generated policy path and runtime watcher path aligned; the intended VSebCode vendor segment is a maintainer identity choice.
Preserve newer watcher functionality. Do not restore AI managed-settings paths, change copyright headers, or copy the VSCodium identity literally.

activation: Active root *.patch: all qualities and preparation host OSes, in shell-glob order after root JSON removals and before Insider/OS/user patches. Effective only for the surviving target surface.
effect: Builds explicit request options for the extension control manifest and adds Connection: close for non-web requests before calling requestService.request. VSebCode retains the GET with timeout and callSite but does not set the connection-close header. Its control URL intentionally remains the Microsoft Marketplace control manifest, whereas VSCodium configures its own control file.

activation: Active only when VSCODE_QUALITY=insider, after all root patches and before OS/user patches.
effect: In VSCodium Insider builds, removes the stable-quality condition from the system-extension outdated guard while retaining its product auto-update allowlist exception. That prevents unallowlisted system extensions from being considered outdated on Insider too. VSebCode has no maintained Insider distribution and intentionally removed the AI-oriented product allowlist, but its remaining guard still checks quality===stable. Its tracked product has no quality field, so an undefined-quality build is not covered by that guard either; this is not equivalent quality-independent behavior.
gaps: No current Insider release requirement is established. If quality-independent system-extension blocking is desired for fork development or future Insider builds, the behavior is absent and should be decided explicitly.
